newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico City declares air pollution alert.
newsitem.headline: Mexico City declares air pollution alert.

text.p: Mexico City officials declared a smog emergency on Tuesday, ordering schoolchildren indoors, urging factories to cut production and implementing a plan that will keep hundreds of motorists off city streets.

Air pollution levels soared to dangerous levels as a lack of wind trapped foul air in the city's bowl-shaped valley. Levels of ozone in parts of the giant metropolis reached 262 points on the local IMECA scale, nearly three times international limits.

Officials doubled the daily "no driving" programme, which will keep nearly half the city's cars off the streets on Wednesday. Normally, all cars in the city have one day a week on which they cannot drive.

Ozone is a pollutant created when car fumes mix with solar radiation. At 7,400 feet (2,250 metres), Mexico City is especially at risk because of higher solar radiation, the ring of mountains that trap air and more than 3 million cars that are on average a decade old.
